summary.name: The Morning Paper on Operability
summary.one_liner: A blog post transcript of Adrian Colyer's Operability.io talk surveying computer science research papers relevant to operating modern distributed systems.
use_cases: Finding research papers on operating distributed systems
Diagnosing bugs that only occur in production
summary.what_it_does: This is a blog post transcribing a 30-minute talk that reviews research papers relevant to operability. It covers James Hamilton's paper on designing internet-scale services, tracing and log-based approaches such as Dapper, The Mystery Machine, lprof and Pivot Tracing, and root-cause tools such as Gist, delta debugging, DEMi and DBSherlock. It also discusses feedback-driven development and the paper How Complex Systems Fail. The post summarizes key findings and results from each paper rather than presenting new research.
notable: Summarizes many papers on distributed tracing, failure diagnosis and test minimization in one place
Includes a delta debugging example that shrinks a C program and an HTML document to minimal reproductions
Links to a checklist gist derived from Hamilton's paper
caveats: Contains no new research; it is a retrospective of previously reviewed papers
Many described systems (Gist, DEMi, lprof, DBSherlock) are research prototypes whose availability is not fully stated on the page
